summary.headline: Mitsu Chem Plast Q1 FY27 net profit rose 566% YoY to INR 873.83 lakhs on a 16.29% EBITDA margin, with total income up 11.62%.
summary.overview:
Total income reached INR 9,532.78 lakhs (+11.62% YoY) and EBITDA INR 1,549.48 lakhs (+209.50% YoY), with margin expanding to 16.29% from 5.87%. Net profit of INR 873.83 lakhs was up sequentially from INR 771.73 lakhs in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the gain to operating efficiency and product mix, and announced a proposed 3,550 MTPA capacity addition on top of 32,450 MTPA. Management said it now prioritises bottom line over top line, and that the INR 1,000 crore revenue target by FY28 remains in place.</overview>

segments.name: Packaging (containers, paint containers, jerry cans, caps and closures)
segments.commentary: Management says packaging is about 80% of business and will remain the largest contributor; the 80:20 split with furniture/other parts is expected to hold to INR 1,000 crores. Containers described as in strong demand.

segments.name: Healthcare furniture (Furnastra brand) and other parts
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 19.8% of the business per management, including furniture parts and other parts. Management expects faster growth here than in containers, but gave no target mix.

guidance_outlook: Management expects sequential revenue growth of roughly the same rate each quarter, 'almost same', while focusing more on bottom line.
Sustainable EBITDA margin described as 10-13% on average; management said double-digit EBITDA will remain, with quarterly variation from product mix.
INR 1,000 crore annual revenue target by FY28 reiterated; management says it is in line with the capacity expansion.
IBC (intermediate bulk container) project expected to start commercial production around Q3 FY27; investment amount not yet disclosed.
Proposed 3,550 MTPA capacity addition: management stated capex of approximately INR 2 crore and that the capacity is already online. Revenue contribution to be announced soon.
Management expects utilisation to stay around 64-65%, or about 70% as a healthier level.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity above 32,450 MTPA across four facilities, with 53 blow moulding and 22 injection moulding machines.
Proposed addition of 3,550 MTPA, to be used across all three verticals (containers, furniture parts and others).

Capex for the 3,550 MTPA addition stated as approximately INR 2 crore (the transcript figure, which looks low for this capacity and should be verified); funding is a mix of internal accruals and debt. Management said this depends on machinery source.
Lead time from machinery order to commercial operation is about 6-9 months, per management.
Utilisation was 60-64% through FY26; seasonal peaks reach about 85%.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is strong across all verticals, with containers in particular high demand.

Raw material prices rising on geopolitical and crude-linked pressures; management says suppliers have raised prices and customers have accepted pass-through, with local sourcing used since imports were stopped years ago.
Raw material pass-through to customers is generally on a one-month lag; specialised cases are negotiated individually.
Pricing is a cost-plus markup on raw material; management said other value-add and efficiency gains drive the margin, not the pass-through alone.

Company is rationalising SKUs (around 500) by dropping low-margin products; added more than 30 customers in Q1 and more than 150 in the last year (the two figures were stated inconsistently on the call; the 150 figure is probably cumulative for the year).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion to about 16%, and is it sustainable given raw material pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited innovation, manufacturing efficiency and product mix, and said raw material increases are passed to customers. It later said sustainable margins are 10-13%, with some quarters higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex for the 3,500 MTPA expansion and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approximately INR 2 crore, funded by a mix of internal accruals and debt, and that the capacity is already online.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue growth is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly the same sequential growth each quarter, while focusing more on profit than revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Does a 16% EBITDA margin represent a new normal, and how does the pass-through work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-12% is the normal range and double-digit margins will remain, with pass-through about one month in arrears.

qa_highlights.question: Why add capacity when utilisation is only 64%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said machinery lead time plus 6-9 months of set-up requires planning ahead; utilisation is seasonal, reaching about 85% at peak.

qa_highlights.question: Which businesses will drive the INR 1,000 crore target, and what is the IBC project?
qa_highlights.answer: Packaging remains about 80% and the mix is expected to stay around 80:20. IBC commercial production is expected around Q3, on new machinery with the cost not yet disclosed.

risks_watch: Raw material cost inflation linked to geopolitical and crude-price moves; pass-through is one month in arrears, which can squeeze margins during rapid price rises.
Margin sustainability: Q1's 16.29% is well above the 10-12% range management described as normal, and EBITDA has been volatile quarter to quarter.
The FY28 INR 1,000 crore target needs a sharp step-up. Quarterly revenue is about INR 95 crore, so the run rate needs to reach roughly INR 120-130 crore per quarter or more.
Capex disclosure is thin: the INR 2 crore figure for 3,550 MTPA looks low, and the IBC project cost and the revenue from new capacity are both still undisclosed.
Low export share (about 2%) and an unquantified international healthcare contract; ramp-up timing unclear.
Governance: the warrant allottee (Rikhav Securities) was questioned; management said it was a small investor with no existing relationship, and the warrant proceeds are for working capital.
Utilisation of 64% against a 3,550 MTPA addition; management expects utilisation to remain about 64-65%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and demand, but often vague or deflective on numbers: capex, the IBC investment, the revenue from new capacity and the Furnastra international timeline were all left for later disclosure. Management repeatedly pointed to the bottom line over top-line growth. Audio problems on the call also made several questions hard to hear.
key_quotes: But double-digit EBITDA will remain the same for sure.
